idiom_name: predicate gate between one input and one output channel, criterion carried as data
implementation_notes: Language-neutral blueprint: read a message, evaluate a criterion, act on a single branch - forward matches to the one output channel, discard the rest (or hand them to a discard channel). Keep the criterion a pure function of the message and carry it as data (rule, selector, predicate value) so interest changes without touching the consumer, and prefer header or metadata criteria over body inspection, because everything you inspect you must first receive and parse. Make the discard observable (counts, audit channel) and settle or acknowledge rejected messages exactly as the transport requires. In most languages the structure degenerates into a stdlib higher-order function or a broker rule; write the component by hand only when criteria are configured, composed, reused or named.
code_sketch:
loop:
    msg = channel.receive()
    if criterion(msg):        # header/key first, body only if unavoidable
        output.send(msg)      # the single output channel
    else:
        dropped += 1          # or discard_channel.send(msg)
        channel.settle(msg)   # ack/commit the reject, never leave it locked
pitfalls: Filtering after deserialisation pays the full cost for messages that are then discarded.
A criterion hard-coded in the consumer can neither be reconfigured nor reused by sibling consumers.
Silent drops with no counter turn a too-strict rule into an invisible outage.
Treating the filter as an authorization boundary rather than a routing convenience.

Wrong move: Parse every full message body before deciding interest -> the application pays deserialisation and predicate cost for traffic that will be discarded -> instead filter on headers, routing keys or broker-visible properties first.

Wrong move: Treat a subscription filter as tenant authorization -> a misconfigured rule or alternate subscription can expose data -> instead enforce deny-by-default ACLs at the trust boundary and use filtering only to reduce delivery.

Wrong move: Change a predicate without observing its match rate -> an over-strict rule looks like a consumer outage and discarded messages may be unrecoverable -> instead version and stage criteria, monitor accepted/rejected counts, and retain rejects when replay matters.
